response.sql: WITH order_fills AS (SELECT oe.ordersmark, o.timespan, AVG(oe.fillcount) AS order_avg_fill FROM orderexecutions oe JOIN orders o ON oe.ordersmark = o.recordvault GROUP BY oe.ordersmark, o.timespan), timespan_stats AS (SELECT timespan, AVG(order_avg_fill) AS timespan_avg_fill FROM order_fills GROUP BY timespan), filtered_orders AS (SELECT of.ordersmark, of.timespan, of.order_avg_fill, ts.timespan_avg_fill, of.order_avg_fill - ts.timespan_avg_fill AS above_amount FROM order_fills of JOIN timespan_stats ts ON of.timespan = ts.timespan WHERE of.order_avg_fill > ts.timespan_avg_fill), ranked_orders AS (SELECT ordersmark, timespan, order_avg_fill, above_amount, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY timespan ORDER BY order_avg_fill DESC NULLS LAST) AS rank FROM filtered_orders) SELECT ordersmark, timespan, order_avg_fill, above_amount, rank FROM ranked_orders WHERE rank <= 3 ORDER BY timespan, rank

assumptions.assumption: Each order's average fill is the mean of its fillcount values across matched executions. The timespan's average fill is the mean of order-level averages within that timespan (unweighted by execution count).
Orders with no matched executions are excluded; only orders joined to at least one execution are considered.

alternatives.interpretation: Calculate each timespan's average fill as the direct mean of all fillcount values across all executions (not as the mean of order-level averages), weighting orders by their execution count.
